ai-workspace

Workspace mission

A local-first home for running many agent-assisted projects in parallel without losing the thread — where any session, human or agent, can open at the root and know exactly where everything stands.

The durable why behind the rules in CLAUDE.md and the workflows in HANDBOOK.md. Live state lives in PROJECTS.md.

01Mission

ai-workspace is a local-only management layer that lets one person run many agent-assisted software projects side by side without anything getting lost between sessions. Scattered terminals forget; chat context evaporates; parallel projects blur together. This workspace is the antidote: a calm root with a fixed storage model, a per-project memory, and a deterministic lifecycle an agent can operate.

north star: one calm root an agent can drive, where no project's knowledge is ever lost
  Kepler's half: the calm root — tiers, junctions, index, lifecycle; this machine's shape  (the manager · versioned as the skeleton commit)
  gravity's half: the knowledge never lost — protocol + instruments travel with each project, so a clone self-describes off-workspace  (the protocol · SemVer'd in gravity/)
first wedge: junction tier model + handoff docs + lifecycle slash commands  (shipped — v1.x)
second wedge: mechanical walls for every rule that matters — checkers, gates, tagged SPECs, the patch-loop  (shipped — v2.x/v3.x)
now: portability — a project carries its own protocol and instruments, so a clone renders and
      checks itself on a machine that has never seen this workspace  (protocol half shipped v3.2.1; the manager half reconstructs the shell — bootstrap.py, junction/symlink parity. What's left is proving it under Linux/WSL end to end.)
later shape: OPEN: awaiting the next real failure mode — the walls and portability horizons are
      claimed, and inventing a third would violate §06's admission test.
Rules vs why. CLAUDE.md says what to do; this file says why it's worth doing. When a rule feels arbitrary, the justification should be here — and when the mission changes, the rules follow, not the reverse.

02Why This Shape

The workspace earns its discipline with three moves, each aimed at a specific way multi-project work falls apart:

Failure it preventsThe move
"Where do the real files live, and what's active?"Separate storage from views — canonical files in repos/, activity expressed as junction views in tiers.
"What was I doing here last week?"Every project carries its own memory — CLAUDE.md (identity) + CONTEXT.md (rolling now), read at session start.
"Did I run those setup steps right?"Automate the lifecycle — slash commands + helper scripts, so create / ship / move / triage are deterministic, not hand-typed shell.
"Did the agent actually do it right, or just say it did?"Mechanical walls over prose promises — checkers (check.py), gates that refuse red code, enforcement-tagged SPECs, the patch-loop's anchored rollback. A rule an agent can violate silently isn't a rule; it's a wish.

03Principles

  • The root versions the shell, never the contents. The root is a git repo, but its .gitignore denies * and whitelists only the portable skeleton — the meta files, gravity/, and .claude/ tooling. Every tier folder stays denied, so the workspace can be replicated onto another machine without ever becoming an umbrella repo of your projects. Project version control lives per project, inside repos/<name>/, with its own remote. (The live index, PROJECTS.md, is git-ignored — it names private work; only the sanitized sample ships.)
  • Storage vs views. repos/ is the one canonical store; tiers are cheap junction views. Changing a project's tier is a metadata move, never a file copy.
  • The docs are the memory. CLAUDE.md is stable identity (auto-loads); CONTEXT.md is a rolling snapshot of now. git is the changelog — so CONTEXT.md stays small and never becomes a log.
  • One venv per project. No shared or root-level .venv; silent version collisions are the enemy.
  • The lifecycle is agent-operated and deterministic. Prefer slash commands and argv-driven helper scripts over hand-run shell strings — quoting pitfalls (e.g. junction creation) are designed out, not worked around.
  • One index of record. PROJECTS.md is the single source of truth for which tier each project lives in; it's updated on every transition.
  • Right-sized ceremony. Two docs for most projects; the optional four-doc pipeline only for ambitious ones; stable projects carry a single reactivation trigger instead of a task list.
  • Walls, not wishes. Wherever a rule matters, gravity builds the mechanical wall that catches its violation — a checker, a gate, a tagged test — instead of trusting an agent's prose compliance ("built so a weaker agent can't…"). Corollary: intent graduates to contract only by earning a wall — a scenario enters a PLAN as given/when/then and becomes a SPEC Behavioral Contract line only when a named test asserts it; bugs enter the same door as currently-false scenarios.

04Architecture Principle

Everything reduces to one idea: real files in repos/, junction views in tiers. Lifecycle commands, triage, and the dashboard all operate on that single model — so a new capability extends the storage/view split rather than inventing a parallel notion of "where a project is."

# canonical storage — the only place real files (.git, .venv, code) live
repos/<project>/
      ^
      |  directory junction  (mklink /J on Windows  ·  symlink on Linux/WSL)
      |     via .claude/scripts/link_project.py — argv-driven, no shell quoting
      |
active/  stable/  dormant/  archive/   # views — a project's tier = its lifecycle state
      |
      v
slash commands · /triage · /dashboard · /mission   # all read this one model

(Every tier holds junctions — no exceptions. stable/ is the tier for projects that shipped well: staleness rules don't apply there, because a working system's silence is success, not neglect.)

05The Doc System

The workspace runs on documents with distinct, non-overlapping jobs — at the root, and inside each project. Since v3.0.0 they belong to two named products: Kepler, this manager (tiers, junctions, the index, the dashboard — this machine only), and gravity, the portable protocol a project adopts, which lives whole in gravity/ and is versioned apart. The seam is the reason the now horizon is reachable at all: everything a cloned project needs travels with it.

DocumentScopeJob
CLAUDE.mdrootThe rules and invariants an agent must follow. Auto-loads every session.
MISSION.htmlrootThis file — the durable why behind those rules.
HANDBOOK.mdrootHuman-facing workflows, slash-command reference, glossary.
PROJECTS.mdrootThe live index — which project is in which tier, and its current focus.
CLAUDE.md · CONTEXT.mdper projectStable identity + rolling now. The mandatory pair every project carries.
MISSION.html · IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.mdper projectOptional "four-doc pipeline" for ambitious projects — durable why + phase roadmap (CLAUDE.md §6).
gravity/GRAVITY-PROTOCOL.mddistributionThe canonical project-side protocol. Copied verbatim to <project>/.gravity/GRAVITY.md at adoption, so an independent repo is self-describing to an agent that never sees this workspace. Protocol rules live only here; workspace rules are never embedded in it.
gravity/GRAVITY-GUIDE.htmldistributionThe same protocol, for a human. Copied verbatim to <project>/.gravity/GRAVITY.html in the same breath as the card, so a person who opens an independent repo finds a browser-read guide — what gravity covers, the arc from a user meeting to a verified report, and a phrasebook of what to ask an agent for — instead of only the agent's contract. Ships with a Korean sibling (.ko.html); unstamped — the card carries the version for the family.
gravity/lib/distributionThe portable instruments — installed verbatim into <project>/.gravity/_lib/, so a clone renders and checks itself off-workspace. Re-copy to upgrade; never hand-edit an installed module.
.gravity/<domain>/per projectWhere the heavy docs go when a project outgrows a flat root — one folder per subject domain, routed by .gravity/ROUTER.md. Recognized only when present, never mandated.

Lifecycle is driven by workspace slash commands — /init-project, /ship, /retire, /triage, /dashboard, /mission — defined in .claude/commands/ and backed by helper scripts in .claude/scripts/.

06Non-Goals

  • Do not track any project from the root repo — no umbrella / monorepo. The root's whitelist covers the skeleton only; projects stay independently versioned. Adding a tier folder to it is the one change that would break this.
  • Do not create a shared or root-level .venv.
  • Do not put real project files inside active/, stable/, dormant/, or archive/ — tier folders hold junctions only.
  • The workspace does not manage credentials or secrets; that stays with each project and the local toolchain.
  • CONTEXT.md is not a changelog — never duplicate git history into it.
  • Do not grow ceremony where it doesn't pay: small and one-shot projects stay on the light setup.
  • Gravity is not an ALM / project-management suite. It covers a lifecycle phase only where knowledge loss between sessions is the failure mode (a bug's repro, a deploy's steps, a rule's wall) — never sprints, boards, estimates, a CI service, or metrics dashboards. That knowledge doesn't evaporate; it just doesn't belong here.
Maintenance rule. Edit this file only when the workspace's purpose or a durable principle changes. Operational rules belong in CLAUDE.md; how-to steps belong in HANDBOOK.md; live project state belongs in PROJECTS.md.
